title: 8. Stage 3 vs. Stage 4 Technical Structure, 1W/1D/4H Tape & Breakdown Risk

epigraph.quote: Never argue with a high-volume break below the 50-day and 30-week moving averages in a broad market downtrend; wait for a Stage 1 floor and confirmed turn.
epigraph.author: Weinstein & Minervini Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: Monster's November 20, 2026 tape broke sharply lower from the prior week. Shares fell from $46.46 on November 13 to $43.69 (-0.57% daily, -4.48% to -5.96% weekly) [26][42]. Volume surged to 16.66 million shares (1.62x 20-day / 1.63x 30-day / 1.71x Finviz average), signaling active distribution [42]. Our two market ledgers split on stage classification. The market-facts ledger tags Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) because $43.69 sits $0.19 above the 200-day SMA ($43.50) and $0.18 above the 20-day low ($43.51) [42]. Meanwhile, live TradingView snapshots tag STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, CAP_REJECTED) because shares closed -2.65% below the 50-day SMA ($44.88) and -3.79% below the 30-week SMA ($45.41) [42].

When ledgers diverge, our stricter STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) rule governs new capital. The 4-hour chart confirms weak momentum in a DISLOCATION_AT_MAJOR_SHELF setup with no confirmed 4H turn (intraday_4h_turn: false). Four-hour RSI sits at 34.21 while price ($43.69) trades below the 4H 20-EMA ($45.15) and 4H 50-SMA ($46.23) [42]. Daily RSI sits at 40.00 (weekly 47.36) with ATR(14) at $1.23 and Bollinger width at 11.86%. Macro conditions also worsened: the S&P 500 sits in a Downtrend with 38.8% above 50-DMA, 10 distribution days, and zero of nine sectors above 20-DMA.

web_blocks.takeaway: Heavy 1.62x–1.71x volume pushed MNST below its 50-day and 30-week averages into STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) with no 4H turn inside a Downtrend.

web_blocks.html: Support math at $43.69 confirms why bidding the 200-day shelf fails our anti-hedging gate. The snapshot band ($42.64–$43.94) places its stop ($42.67) inside the band itself. A genuine technical monitor shelf (not a fundamental valuation floor) spans $42.50 to $43.50 across Pivot S1 ($43.29), the 40-week EMA ($43.42), and the 200-day SMA ($43.50). Setting a structural stop 0.5x ATR14 ($0.62) below the 63-day base low ($41.05) yields $40.43. Entering at $43.50 risks $3.07 (-7.06%) for $2.50 of Base upside to $46.00 (+5.75%). That 0.81:1 reward-to-risk ratio fails our 1.50:1 hurdle.

Options liquidity offers no alternative path. Our options snapshot flags MNST as NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID because bid-ask spreads exceed 14% or open interest is thin. Short interest sits at 3.36% of float (46.72M shares, 4.78 days to cover), offering no squeeze catalyst [42]. Until MNST forms a Stage 1 base above $40.43 and reclaims its 50-day ($44.88) and 30-week ($45.41) averages, capital stays on the sidelines.

book_subsections.title: Why the Tape Broke: From Stage 3 Consolidation to Stage 4 Warning
paragraphs: One week ago, Monster Beverage sat at $46.46 in a tight Stage 3 consolidation above its 50-day moving average. By the November 20, 2026 close, that calm dissolved. Shares dropped to $43.69, losing nearly 6% on the week on 16.66 million shares—roughly 1.62 to 1.71 times normal daily volume. Expanding volume on declining prices is the classic footprint of institutional distribution rather than quiet profit-taking.

Look across the daily and weekly moving-average stack to see how much technical damage occurred in a single week. Price now sits 5.01% below the 20-day SMA ($46.00), 2.65% below the 50-day SMA ($44.88), 3.55% below the 10-week EMA ($45.30), and 3.79% below the 30-week SMA ($45.41). Over one month, shares have dropped 6.24% to 7.63%; over three months, they are down 8.21% to 10.69%, sitting 12.92% below the $50.17 52-week high.

Because price now sits right on a technical knife-edge, our two quantitative feeds classify the stock slightly differently. The market-facts ledger still tags Monster as Stage 3 Topping because $43.69 rests nineteen cents above its rising 200-day moving average ($43.50) and eighteen cents above its 20-day swing low ($43.51). However, our TradingView snapshot engine classifies Monster as Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) because shares broke decisively below both the 50-day SMA and the 30-week SMA, driving TradingView's moving-average rating down to -0.67.

When technical models diverge at a major shelf, risk management demands respecting the stricter warning. Worse, the four-hour intraday chart shows zero sign of stabilization: four-hour RSI sits at an oversold 34.21, price remains trapped below the four-hour 20-EMA ($45.15) and four-hour 50-SMA ($46.23), and our intraday turn flag reads false. Catching a falling knife right as the broader S&P 500 enters a 10-distribution-day Downtrend—with just 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day averages and zero of nine sectors above their 20-day averages—invites unnecessary drawdown.

book_subsections.title: Support Math, Illiquid Options, and Why the Hurdle Fails
paragraphs: Even if an investor wanted to bid near the 200-day moving average, the reward-to-risk arithmetic fails our discipline. Note that the automated scanner band ($42.64 to $43.94) actually places its mechanical stop ($42.67) inside the support zone itself, which creates an unworkably tight stop less than one ATR wide. A realistic structural support zone runs from $42.50 to $43.50, capturing Pivot S1 ($43.29), the 40-week EMA ($43.42), and the 200-day SMA ($43.50). To avoid getting shaken out by daily volatility—where 14-day ATR equals $1.23—a true structural stop must sit half an ATR below the 63-day base low of $41.05, placing invalidation at $40.43.

Compare that $3.07 downside risk from $43.50 against our freshly audited $46.00 Base Target. Upside from $43.50 to $46.00 is just $2.50, creating a sub-unit 0.81-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Even from the $42.50 bottom of the shelf, risk-reward barely reaches 1.69-to-1 while sitting inside a Stage 4 breakdown and a market Downtrend. Below $40.43, the next major technical floor does not arrive until Pivot S2 at $39.25.

Monster's options market provides zero relief from this poor equity setup. Our options engine flags Monster as NOT OPTIONABLE OR ILLIQUID because listed spreads exceed 14% or lack adequate open interest, forbidding defined-risk call overlays to avoid slippage. Short interest sits at a modest 3.36% of float (46.72 million shares, or 4.78 days to cover), offering no short-squeeze cushion either. In short, the tape confirms what our valuation model already signaled: step aside and demand either a real Stage 1 base or a deeper valuation reset.

callouts.title: The Discipline of Letting Price Prove Support
callouts.text: Touching a 200-day moving average on 1.7x volume is not support—holding that level, shrinking selling volume, and turning higher on the 4-hour and daily charts is support. Until buyers step up, $43.50 is a test, not a floor.

book_subsections.title: Mapping Overhead Resistance and What a True Reset Looks Like
paragraphs: To know when Monster becomes actionable again, map the exact overhead supply waiting above $43.69. Any reflexive bounce must first clear the falling 50-day SMA at $44.88, the 4-hour 20-EMA at $45.15, the 10-week EMA at $45.30, and the 30-week SMA at $45.41. Beyond those moving averages sit the 20-day SMA ($46.00), Pivot R1 ($49.50), and the 52-week peak at $50.17.

In a healthy Stage 2 reset, we do not need to guess the exact bottom tick. First, Monster must stop making lower lows above $40.43 and let its 11.86% Bollinger bandwidth contract as selling volume dries up below average. Second, price must reclaim both the 50-day and 30-week averages on above-average institutional accumulation, turning the 4-hour and daily momentum indicators back upward. Third, the broader S&P 500 must heal from its 10-distribution-day Downtrend toward healthier breadth. Until those signals appear together, sitting in cash costs nothing and preserves full optionality.

Checking the broader sector backdrop reinforces that caution. Inside our market-facts ledger, zero of nine tracked US sectors currently trade above their 20-day moving averages, and only two of nine hold above their 50-day and 200-day averages. Even defensive consumer staples are seeing selective rotation rather than broad accumulation: Coca-Cola ($96.99) and PepsiCo ($140.54) hold Stage 2 trends above their 50-day averages, whereas high-multiple Monster ($43.69) and leveraged challenger Celsius ($28.46) have both slipped into Stage 4 snapshot readings.

When institutional allocators de-risk high-beta and high-multiple equities simultaneously during a ten-distribution-day Downtrend, single-stock 200-day moving averages frequently act as temporary speed bumps rather than durable floors. Respecting the Stage 4 snapshot ceiling protects capital from getting caught in a secondary leg down toward Pivot S2 at $39.25.

Notice also how Monster's own distribution-day count corroborates the weekly breakdown. Over the trailing twenty-five sessions, Monster logged four institutional distribution days on its own chart while relative volume on November 20 surged to 1.62x–1.71x normal turnover. Combined with an expanding 11.86% Bollinger bandwidth and a negative 4-hour trend slope (4H EMA20 at $45.15 below 4H SMA50 at $46.23), sellers remain firmly in control of short-term price discovery.

Even the $43.50 200-day moving average carries less cushion than it appears at first glance. On November 20, daily RSI dropped to 40.00 and weekly RSI fell to 47.36, both pointing lower without any positive divergence on the four-hour chart. When a high-multiple stock tests its 200-day average on 1.7x volume after a 6% weekly drop, waiting for sellers to exhaust themselves near $41.05 to $43.50 avoids stepping in front of forced institutional liquidation.

If selling pressure breaks cleanly below the 200-day moving average ($43.50) and Pivot S1 ($43.29) over the coming sessions, the next horizontal demand zone sits at the 63-day base low of $41.05, followed by our $40.43 reference invalidation stop and Pivot S2 at $39.25. Patience keeps capital completely shielded from that markdown risk while allowing us to observe whether institutional buyers finally step in around $39 to $41.
